paragraphs: According to a new report, Upper Fifth Avenue in New York is once again the most expensive shopping street in the world. The report comes from Cushman & Wakefield, a property company, and it came out on Wednesday. Rents on the street went up 35 percent over the past year, to 2,700 dollars per square foot each year.

This is a remarkable return. In 2025, Fifth Avenue was in third place. Now it is first, for the first time since 2023. London's New Bond Street is second, at 2,230 dollars per square foot. Milan's Via Montenapoleone comes next, at 2,160 dollars. Rents on these two rivals stayed flat over the past year. In last year's report, New Bond Street was at the top.

Rents there jumped because of strong demand and very little spare space. In February, FashionUnited reported that luxury groups had spent nearly 4 billion dollars on property there over two years. Kering paid almost 1 billion dollars for one building. Rolex is constructing a store with 30 floors. Constructing it will cost 250 million dollars. The city is also spending 400 million dollars on a transformation of the street. This transformation is called "Future of Fifth."

Spare space is hard to find in Manhattan. Another company, JLL, measures the availability of stores on its top shopping streets. At the end of 2025, availability fell to 13.7 percent, the lowest level since 2017. Dominic Brown of Cushman & Wakefield said that rents can go up very quickly when strong demand meets low availability.

The report has a wide scope: 147 shopping streets around the world. Across this scope, rents went up 3 percent on average compared with a year earlier, in local money. That is slower than 4.3 percent in 2025, but still steady. Rents went up on 49 percent of the streets, fell on 19 percent and stayed the same on 32 percent.

Fashion is the main force behind this phenomenon. On the top 30 streets, fashion companies made 50 percent of the lease deals. They also took the bulk of the space, 57 percent. Brands from other countries took about 90 percent of the space, so foreign brands took the bulk.

Why do brands pay so much? Alanna Loeffler of Cushman & Wakefield said that a big store today is more than a place to buy and sell. It helps to build the brand and brings more interaction with customers. This interaction can keep customers for a long time. According to her, the intensity of the competition for the best locations has never been higher. Dominic Brown also spoke about the intensity of the competition for space in the best destinations.

The phenomenon is not only on the most famous streets. Rents went up 43 percent on Brickell Boulevard in Miami and 28 percent on Linking Road in Mumbai. In London, rents on Regent Street and in Covent Garden each went up 13 percent.
